gaps.sentence: He's always been fascinated by ___ universe.
I live on ___ Baker Street, near the tube station.
gaps.explanation: Street names take no article: Baker Street, Oxford Street.

gaps.sentence: ___ Himalayas are among the youngest mountains on Earth.
gaps.explanation: Ranges like 'the Himalayas' take 'the'; single peaks take no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ Alps attract skiers from all over the world.
gaps.explanation: Mountain ranges take 'the' (the Alps), but single peaks take no article (Everest).

gaps.sentence: ___ noise woke me up in the middle of the night.
gaps.explanation: 'The noise' — the one that woke me; 'in the night' is a fixed phrase.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

gaps.sentence: ___ influenza, or flu, is highly contagious.
gaps.explanation: Most disease names take no article: influenza, flu, malaria (compare: the flu is also heard informally).

gaps.sentence: He left ___ school at sixteen and went straight into a job.
gaps.explanation: Leave school (finish education) takes no article.
